The measured m59 points 036352f6818925e928f6 and 76435080f7632be26e64 were much earlier and narrower than predicted, while c4b06a6e718225cb9cf8 supports a separate late aromatic-aldehyde regime. The m181 result 3163a9b58f1a52a1992c and the simple ester result 071fc2962498be2a0922 confirm that carbonyl topology matters. The m72 weak-eluent point ce8391d5c053e7fad6e4 overpredicted V2, so the enamine curve needs anchors rather than monotone extrapolation. The m96 result 0be038db2251642c6862 was close to prediction, and the earlier 20/1 points a0fb13951a097b6a1516 and 8b0153f031bc52c2c1dd did not support a universal loading-width correction. The batch therefore emphasizes ratio curves around m107, m59, m177, m199, m125, m96, and nitrogen families, with matched loading contrasts and neutral controls.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several measured failure regions while preserving scientifically meaningful local experiments. Four m107 points map the oxygen-rich carbonyl response from weak to intermediate eluent; m59 and m177 points test whether recent aromatic-carbonyl failures are smooth curves or regime shifts; m199 and m96 points probe sulfur and heteroatom transfer; and m90, m161, and m146 points extend nitrogen-specific responses. m125, m205, and m206 add oxygen-placement and alcohol topology contrasts. The m17, m14, and m210 controls constrain corrections on ordinary ester and donor-free aromatic rows. These labels should improve generalization across the Row-distribution by teaching separate V1 and V2 response components, identifying where loading effects are conditional, and limiting transfer of broad-tail corrections into compact molecules."}
